correctness.rationale: For any p≥17 each local bad-index mask in a 14-window is empty, a singleton or two neighboring indices; the explicit finite superset suffices. Every allowed 3-odd-prime support maps to one of 26 combinations of five exact small-prime mask sets and the large superset. The standalone script exhaustively computes all products and union bitmasks, showing exactly two 14-coverings, both with small support 3,5,7. CRT/direct period enumeration gives a=2,89 mod 105, and their good neighboring starts exclude length 15. The code was executed from the packaged content path, and the table is included in the proof. No finite sample inference is substituted for the exact reduction.

value.rationale: The three-prime layer is a canonical small-support level in paired Jacobsthal and wheel-sieve problems. It has a nontrivial jump in attainable blocked-run lengths and a sharp uniform cutoff valid for arbitrary large prime factors; the uniquely extremal 3·5·7 support and exact two CRT start classes are a natural complete classification. The result controls finite gaps between admissible adjacent pairs and is not a parameter substitution, bounded scan of moduli, or restatement of an existing table. It makes no unjustified claim about prime-pair existence.
